verdicts.claim: RoomPlan and your own ARKit mesh/depth pipeline can run on ONE ARSession: `RoomCaptureSession(arSession:)` (iOS 17) accepts your ARSession; RoomPlan 'honors any custom ARSession with ARWorldTrackingConfiguration' (WWDC23 10192), so your configuration (sceneReconstruction .meshWithClassification, frameSemantics sceneDepth, planeDetection, videoFormat) stays in effect while RoomPlan produces CapturedRoom data, and `stop(pauseARSession: false)` keeps the ARSession running between rooms so multi-room scans share one world coordinate frame (or save/restore ARWorldMap between sessions and wait for relocalization before `run(configuration:)`).
verdicts.correction: Uphold the verifiers on the core point: your ARWorldTrackingConfiguration does NOT reliably stay in effect after `RoomCaptureSession.run(configuration:)`. Rely on this: (1) Declarations (Apple doc JSON, re-fetched): `init(arSession: ARSession? = nil)` on RoomCaptureSession iOS 17.0+; `@MainActor init(frame: CGRect, arSession: ARSession)` on RoomCaptureView iOS 17.0+; `var arSession: ARSession` iOS 16.0+ (set at init, throws if assigned); `func stop(pauseARSession: Bool = true)` iOS 17.0+; `func captureSession(_ session: RoomCaptureSession, didStartWith configuration: RoomCaptureSession.Configuration)` iOS 16.0+; ARSession `weak var delegate: (any ARSessionDelegate)? { get set }` iOS 11.0+. None deprecated on the iOS 26 SDK. (2) Sharing one ARSession works, but RoomPlan re-runs it with its own configuration on run(configuration:) and sceneDepth (and possibly other frameSemantics / videoFormat) disappears. Required pattern: run your own ARWorldTrackingConfiguration (sceneReconstruction .meshWithClassification, frameSemantics .sceneDepth, planeDetection, videoFormat) on the session, create RoomCaptureSession(arSession:), call run(configuration:), then in `captureSession(_:didStartWith:)` call `arSession.run(myConfig)` again with NO options (default options keep tracking state and existing anchors, so the world origin and mesh anchors stay continuous; never pass .resetTracking or .removeExistingAnchors there). Keep a watchdog that re-applies the configuration if `frame.sceneDepth == nil` and log `arSession.configuration` after each RoomPlan start (each room). (3) The RoomCaptureView doc sentence 'If you pass an ARSession instance, RoomPlan preserves all of the AR session's settings' exists verbatim, but it is a parameter note on RoomCaptureView.init(frame:arSession:) only, and practical reports contradict it for the headless RoomCaptureSession path; do not rely on it. (4) Delegate conflict resolved: the app MAY and SHOULD set `arSession.delegate = self` (set it before run()). Reject the reality verifier's 'RoomPlan takes the single delegate slot, do not set it' sub-point: Apple's own article implements ARSessionObserver callbacks for the RoomPlan session, the forum 763400 author (a shipping scanning app) read sceneDepth through the ARSession delegate callback with RoomPlan running once the configuration was re-applied, and many public repos (including Meta's facebookresearch/ocean, which sets it even after run) assign it. Only reading `currentFrame` is a fallback, not a requirement. (5) Multi-room: `stop(pauseARSession: false)` then `run(configuration:)` again on the same RoomCaptureSession is Apple's documented continuous-coordinate-space path; ARWorldMap relocalization is the documented fallback. The re-apply step must be repeated after every run(configuration:).
verdicts.reasoning: Ruling on the official-docs verdict: upheld. Re-fetched doc JSON: roomcaptureview/init(frame:arsession:).json (iOS 17.0; arSession parameter text: 'A world-tracking session that your app creates and runs with an ARWorldTrackingConfiguration before calling this function. If you pass an ARSession instance, RoomPlan preserves all of the AR session's settings.'), roomcapturesession/init(arsession:).json (iOS 17.0), roomcapturesession/arsession.json, capturesession(_:didstartwith:).json (iOS 16.0), arkit/arsession/run(_:options:).json ('By default, the session resumes device position tracking from the last known state and keeps any anchors'), arkit/arsession/delegate.json. The docs never state that RoomCaptureSession's run keeps your frameSemantics; the only 'preserves' sentence is scoped to RoomCaptureView. Against that, I fetched Apple forum thread 763400 itself (Sep 2024, readable this time): 'when we do call run on the RoomCaptureSession, sceneDepth is no longer present on the incoming ARFrames', accepted answer 'This can work by re-running a sceneDepth enabled WorldTrackingConfiguration after the RoomPlanSession's didStart delegate method is invoked'. Corroborated by thread 808834 (Dec 2025, custom ARSession plus arSession.delegate = self, sceneDepth prints nil once RoomPlan runs, unanswered) and thread 710134 (Apr 2023, RoomPlan's session configuration lacks .sceneDepth; a later reply notes configuration changes are not immediate). Thread 728601 (Apr 2023) shows the behavior differs between RoomCaptureView and a bare RoomCaptureSession, which reconciles the 'preserves' doc line with the field reports: it may hold for the view path, it does not hold for the headless session. The claim as written ('stays in effect') is therefore wrong; the verifier's re-apply-in-didStartWith correction is right and is the design to build. I also agree with its secondary note that setting the delegate before init works.

verdicts.reasoning: Ruling on the reality verdict: upheld on sceneDepth being dropped and on the re-apply-in-didStartWith fix (forum 763400 read directly this session, accepted answer as quoted; threads 808834 and 710134 agree). Rejected on one sub-point: 'RoomPlan takes the single ARSession.delegate slot; do not set arSession.delegate yourself'. Evidence against it: (a) Apple's article 'Scanning the rooms of a single structure' (doc JSON re-fetched) shows the app implementing ARSessionObserver `sessionShouldAttemptRelocalization(_:)` and `session(_:cameraDidChangeTrackingState:)` for the RoomPlan AR session, which are only delivered to ARSession.delegate; (b) the 763400 author states they extract sceneDepth 'via the delegate callback' and the accepted fix only re-runs the configuration, implying delegate frames kept flowing with RoomPlan running; (c) GitHub code search for "arSession.delegate = self" RoomCaptureSession returned 18 Swift files, including facebookresearch/ocean AKRoomPlanTracker6DOF_Swift.swift (creates RoomCaptureSession(), calls run(configuration:), then sets `roomCaptureSession_?.arSession.delegate = self` and implements session(_:didUpdate:)), ThomasZhang223/Scale RoomCaptureController.swift (sets arSession.delegate = self, runs mesh + sceneDepth config, then RoomCaptureSession(arSession:)), Brighthammer-App/expo-roomplan. The two sources claiming the delegate breaks SLAM give no reproducible report. Also, the 'no Apple sample configures a custom ARSession with mesh' note is accurate but irrelevant to the ruling. The StackOverflow 79208951 tracking-loss report concerns creating a NEW RoomCaptureView per room; Mapper should reuse one RoomCaptureSession across rooms as Apple's article does, and keep ARWorldMap relocalization as fallback.

open_question_answers.question: Does RoomCaptureSession(arSession:) re-run the ARSession with its own ARWorldTrackingConfiguration (possibly dropping your frameSemantics/videoFormat) when run(configuration:) is called? WWDC23 says a custom session is 'honored'; confirm on device by logging session.configuration after RoomPlan starts.
open_question_answers.answer: Yes in practice. With a custom ARSession passed to RoomCaptureSession(arSession:), run(configuration:) re-runs the session with RoomPlan's own configuration and sceneDepth disappears from ARFrames (forum 763400 Sep 2024, 808834 Dec 2025, 710134 Apr 2023). Fix, accepted on 763400: re-run your sceneDepth-enabled ARWorldTrackingConfiguration inside captureSession(_:didStartWith:), with default (empty) run options so tracking and anchors are preserved. Configuration changes are not immediate, so check a few frames later. The RoomCaptureView.init(frame:arSession:) doc says 'RoomPlan preserves all of the AR session's settings' but that is scoped to the view path and is contradicted for the headless session. Still log on device: arSession.configuration (videoFormat, frameSemantics, sceneReconstruction, planeDetection) before RoomPlan start, right after didStartWith, and after the re-apply, plus frame.sceneDepth != nil rate, for every room of a multi-room scan; also confirm whether videoFormat is replaced.

open_question_answers.question: Does the out-of-band hi-res ARFrame from captureHighResolutionFrame carry sceneDepth? Docs say pose/anchors/frame semantics are populated; developer reports suggest depth may be nil. Test on device.
open_question_answers.answer: Apple staff answer (forum 805839, Nov 2025): with .sceneDepth in frameSemantics you 'should receive depth data through sceneDepth.depthMap on high-resolution frames already with the default photo settings'. `capturedDepthData` is only non-nil for ARFaceTrackingConfiguration (TrueDepth), and passing AVCapturePhotoSettings with isDepthDataDeliveryEnabled = true to captureHighResolutionFrame(using:) throws. So: call `captureHighResolutionFrame(completion:)` (iOS 16.0+) or the async `captureHighResolutionFrame(using: nil)` form, and read `frame.sceneDepth` (expect the regular low-resolution LiDAR depth map, not one matching the photo size, so scale intrinsics; unverified). Still verify on the iPhone 13 Pro Max: log sceneDepth != nil and depthMap dimensions on the hi-res frame, especially while RoomPlan is running (after the re-apply).

open_question_answers.question: Exact mesh chunk extent, vertex spacing and update cadence are undocumented (community: ~1 m square chunks, denser when close). Measure on the iPhone 13 Pro Max to size the mesh store and the export.
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: log per ARMeshAnchor on add/update the vertex count, face count, bounding extent in anchor space, and timestamp deltas between updates, over a 5 minute room scan at normal walking distance and at 0.5 m close-ups; also total anchors and total vertex bytes to size the mesh store. No official figures exist (ARMeshGeometry docs give no chunk size or cadence).

open_question_answers.question: Typical ARWorldMap size for a full apartment scan and relocalization reliability on iOS 18.3 are unmeasured; matters for the 'resume a multi-room scan later' flow.
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: after each room, call getCurrentWorldMap and log archived byte size (NSKeyedArchiver), anchors.count and rawFeaturePoints count; then relaunch, run with initialWorldMap and log time until trackingState is .normal after .limited(.relocalizing), and the success rate across 5 attempts per room under different lighting. Architecture should treat relocalization as best-effort and allow a scan to be resumed as a new, separately aligned segment if it fails.

open_question_answers.question: Whether the reported ARMeshAnchor remove/re-add churn (iPad Pro 4th gen report) also occurs on iPhone 13 Pro Max / iOS 18.3.2.
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: log ARMeshAnchor identifiers in didAdd/didRemove and count identifiers that are removed and later re-added (or replaced) during one scan, with and without RoomPlan running and after the configuration re-apply in didStartWith. Design the mesh store keyed by anchor identifier with remove handling regardless, since removal is a documented delegate event.
